newsitem.title: UK: Chartists see weaker outlook for Swedish crown.
newsitem.headline: Chartists see weaker outlook for Swedish crown.

text.p: The Swedish crown brushed off a report earlier on Wednesday suggesting there would be a lengthy delay to Sweden's EMU membership, but technical analysts said the chart outlook is for the currency to weaken.

Although the mark rose slightly against the crown after the report, it stayed within the recent 4.49-4.53 crowns' band it has traded over the last three days and comfortably within a broader range that has held for the past three months.

"The bias is to (mark/crown) upside," said Karen Jones, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston in London. "It has been base-building for some considerable time -- since January of last year."

A radio report said Sweden's prime minister and finance minister had agreed the government could not join EMU during the current parliamentary term and that a general election would have to be called for Sweden to join monetary union.

Analysts said this meant Swedish EMU membership would be delayed until after the next election in 2002, unless the government took the unusual step of holding an extra election during the 1998-2002 mandate period.
Chartists said mark/crown faces initial significant resistance around 4.5730, a falling trendline drawn from its February 1996 highs.
Above here, the early May top of 4.5815 crowns caps before this year's peak seen in mid-March of 4.6020.
A break above this 4.60 level should then find little in its way until around 4.7335 crowns.
"This is a 38.2 percent Fibonacci retracement of the entire move from the high of 5.4560 in April 1995 to the 4.2870 low of October last year," said CSFB's Jones.
Chartists see limited potential for crown gains against the mark. As well as the constraints of its recent, sideways range, the medium-term trend has been for a higher mark/crown.
"Mark/crown is looking supportive at the moment," said Ian Stannard, technical analyst at Chase Investment Bank here. "The trendline support from October 1996 is still intact."
Stannard sees the bias to the upside, particularly if mark/crown holds above key supports, the first being a trendline in the 4.4355 area and then at the April low around 4.42 crowns.
"But it has to hold above 4.5160. This has been a quite pivotal level with the consolidation of the last three months taking place around here."
